# 1: Project Overview

This project acts as a window into the relationship between a powerlifter's body weight and their overall strength. Is a powerlifter's body weight directly correlated with their compound lift strength (squat + bench press + deadlift)? This project will focus on cleaning the dataset, separating sexes, identifying age and weight classes, and graphing the information to visualize strength standard trends.

## 2.2.1: Data Set Information & Fair Use

**Producer and authority.** OpenPowerlifting.org hosts an open-source, non-profit collection of powerlifting data. It is published as an open dataset to standardize global powerlifting meet results into a single, easy-to-use domain.

**Original Dataset Purpose.** The purpose of OpenPowerlifting.org is to preserve powerlifting data taken from professional meets and to provide a comprehensive archive of athletic accomplishments. It is primarily utilized to track rankings and analyze sports trends among athletes.

**Collection method.** The values are gathered manually from official powerlifting organizations using powerlifting federation score sheets and score-reporting platforms. The provided data is analyzed and structured into a CSV file.

**Coverage and resolution.** This dataset features global coverage across multiple officially licensed powerlifting federations. The data spans from 1964 to the present through continuous competition results.

**Licence.** Creative Commons Zero (CC0 1.0 Universal) Public Domain Dedication, allowing unrestricted use, modification, and distribution for any purpose.

**Access.** Downloaded directly from the OpenPowerlifting.org public Git repository and accessed through OpenPowerlifting.org/data.

**Known problems.** After a brief review, some values are missing. Certain figures required for this project—such as Best3SquatKg, Best3BenchKg, and Best3DeadliftKg—contain null values. Some bodyweight entries are also missing. I may rectify this by providing specific graphs for individual lifts where available if athletes did not compete in all three compound lifts.

# 4: Consent and identifiability

**Consent.** This dataset provides users with individual powerlifters' details, such as names, sex, and age. The data is sourced from open athletic competition results that are part of the public record. In order for these athletes to compete, they must agree to federation rules that record key identifiers such as names, body weights, performance statistics, and doping tests. For the purpose of this project, individual names will not be used in any graph or aggregated analysis.

**Identifiability.** This dataset utilizes publicly recorded athletic statistics, including competition names, body weights, and performance metrics from powerlifting competitions. Because these records are shared publicly, individual identification relies entirely on publicly available competition results. However, this project will not use names; it will analyze only the key physical and performance characteristics of athletes.

**How sensitive data will be used.** Although the OpenPowerlifting dataset includes names and competition data, this project analyzes strength standards at a population level rather than an individual level. Names and specific athletes will not be singled out. All information used in this project will be presented in figures such as summary tables, regression models, and graphs, ensuring that no individual identity is highlighted.
